$comment: The known weaknesses and their real fixes (constitution XI). The one source for the README table (scripts/render-weaknesses.mjs, T103); the app shows no weaknesses screen (spec 004 FR-015). Edit here, then run: node scripts/render-weaknesses.mjs

weaknesses.what: Devnet with a mock SKR mint
weaknesses.why: Hackathon build; no real value at stake
weaknesses.fix: Mainnet with real SKR

weaknesses.what: Seeker ID names and the Seeker Genesis Token are read from Solana mainnet
weaknesses.why: Seeker IDs (.skr names) and Seeker Genesis Tokens exist only on mainnet. The app reads both from the public mainnet RPC: Seeker ID names for display only, and the wallet's Seeker Genesis Token before a join. Everything else runs on devnet. Members without a Seeker ID, scripted members included, are shown by shortened address
weaknesses.fix: Nothing to fix for the names: on mainnet the same lookup reads the same network. At mainnet launch the contract checks the Seeker Genesis Token itself (see the Seeker-exclusive row). A dedicated RPC provider would make first-time lookups of large lists faster

weaknesses.what: "Stake back" is true in SKR, not in dollars
weaknesses.why: Everything is SKR-denominated with no oracle in the contract
weaknesses.fix: A known property of SKR-native staking, stated in the app

weaknesses.what: Staking is Seeker-exclusive, but on devnet the app enforces it, not the contract (`genesis_gate_enabled = false`)
weaknesses.why: Seeker Genesis Tokens exist only on mainnet, so the app checks the wallet's token on mainnet before it offers a join; a wallet that signs a join without the app is not stopped, and a wallet confirmed once is remembered on that phone
weaknesses.fix: Two steps at mainnet launch: turn the flag on, and have the app send the member's Seeker Genesis Token account and its mint as `join_cohort`'s remaining accounts. The contract then checks the token on every join; that check is already written and tested

weaknesses.what: Non-default `day_seconds` for test cohorts — a **short test lobby kept running on devnet**, labelled and open to every Seeker owner, from which the demo video is recorded
weaknesses.why: Lets a single person run a whole cycle alone: three 10-minute days, a new round every 30 minutes, in two lobbies side by side — Hackathon · Spark and Hackathon · Habit (FR-044a, owner 2026-10-13). Both have the same length and cadence, and only the newest test league of each level opens rounds, since streaks are written when a cohort is counted and test leagues of different lengths could count a member's outcomes out of order on the combined test board
weaknesses.fix: Admin-guarded; real cohorts always use 24 hours

weaknesses.what: A completed day's proof is client-signed
weaknesses.why: No backend in the build
weaknesses.fix: Server-side attestation signer with pinned traces

weaknesses.what: Reps banked during the day (in blocks of 10), and a completed day waiting for network, live only on the phone
weaknesses.why: No wallet prompt mid-workout; a lost phone loses that day's partial progress, and a rooted phone could edit it. A day finished offline counts only if it reaches the network before the deadline
weaknesses.fix: Covered by the attestation fix; cross-device progress later

weaknesses.what: Knee push-ups count in the Daily 25 and in Spark Holdouts, by design
weaknesses.why: The Daily 25 and Spark Holdouts **count push-ups from the knees on purpose** — a free habit, and a 7-day Holdout, for building strength; only Habit Holdouts refuse them. Every sitting is counted at 45° since 8 Oct, and the Daily 25 is held to the Spark set-up: until then it also accepted the phone head-on, where the legs and hips point into the lens and knee angle, knee and ankle height, hip height, torso angle and body line all read the same for knee push-ups as for honest ones (`fixtures/rep-traces/front-knees-01`), so it counted there what a Holdout refuses
weaknesses.fix: Nothing to fix for the knees: the Daily 25 shows how many of the day's reps came from the toes, so a member can see how far they are from a Habit

weaknesses.what: At 45° the body line is checked only coarsely, and the knee rule is 'off the floor'
weaknesses.why: Recorded on the phone, honest planks read 152–167° at 45°, so the ±10° body-line rule cannot be measured there; a rep is refused only when its median body line folds below 140°. In staked sittings, knees are judged on the push back up, mainly by how high the knee and ankle stand above the hands (honest 0.44–0.65 arm-lengths, knees down 0.32–0.39, line at 0.41), with the knee angle (below 90°: a deep kneel, or the feet raised behind) as a second signal — a leg bent in the air is allowed. The lines were set on one person's recordings, with the phone at floor level; the margins are 0.03–0.05. A second person's knee push-ups read the legs over the 0.41 line (0.42–0.44; his honest reps 0.51–0.79), so the legs on the push are also judged against the member's own plank held through the countdown: under 0.66 of it is knees down (honest reps on every recording 0.70 or more, his knee reps 0.60–0.63). Knee push-ups filmed at a flatter angle, nearer head-on, read like honest reps. Knees are judged only while the elbow is above 100°, on the way down and on the push back up: at the bottom the landmarks read honest reps lower than push-ups from the knees (legs 0.27–0.43 against 0.42–0.65), so a rep pushed from the knees through the bottom and back on the toes by 100° is not caught
weaknesses.fix: More recorded sets, especially 45° knee push-ups recorded on the phone; a lower-body classifier if the angle proves too loose

weaknesses.what: Loose trousers hide the knees from the pose model
weaknesses.why: In loose trousers the model cannot find the knee and puts it on the ankle, so nothing about the knee can be judged: a staked sitting does not start, and says so ("Can't see knees"). Measured on one person in loose white trousers — the knee unreadable in 60–67 % of frames, against 0–1 % for fitted clothing
weaknesses.fix: Wear something fitted or roll the trousers up; the knee-on-the-floor image classifier would not depend on the knee landmark

weaknesses.what: A cobra is refused at 45°, but not in every case
weaknesses.why: Lying flat and pressing only the chest up, hips on the floor, counted at 45° until the body line was judged on the push back up (honest 157–174°, cobra 120–134°). A cobra done with the body nearly straight, and a rep pushed up from lying on the floor, passed that check; they are refused by how far the hips have risen half-way up the push against the shoulders (honest 0.92–1.06, those 0.63–0.87, line 0.90) — with a margin of 0.02–0.03, measured on two people; in a staked sitting a rep whose rise cannot be read is not credited. From further in front than about 35° that check does not hold, so no sitting starts there; the Daily 25 and Spark, which accept a body line straight to the ankle **or to the knee** (so knee push-ups with the feet raised count), stop at about 40°. Until 8 Oct the Daily 25 started further in front, and cobras got through there: 4 of 5 on one recording (`angled-mixed-03`). Not caught: a rep let down until the hips rest on the floor and pushed up straight in one piece — no landmark reading tells a hip on the floor from a deep honest bottom (four counted on 4 Oct) — and, on a second person whose head covered the near hand at the bottom, two cobras, because the near wrist was misplaced and every arm reading with it
weaknesses.fix: The knee-on-the-floor image classifier, extended to hips on the floor; a wrist reading that holds when the head covers the near hand

weaknesses.what: No liveness check and no audio anti-spoofing in rep verification
weaknesses.why: The palm-liveness check was dropped on 22 September after the first sitting on real hardware: by the time the checks pass the member is face-down on the floor, and it asked them to lift a hand off it. Holding the top of a push-up starts the sitting instead — a readiness check, not a liveness one. So nothing here tells a live person from a video played to the lens, or one member from another. Microphone permission, which would, adds first-run friction and protects no real value on devnet
weaknesses.fix: Reinstate the audio check and the audio rep condition together — one move restores liveness and anti-spoofing both

weaknesses.what: Stake chips (≈ $10 / $25 / $50 / $100) are priced in SKR by the Operator from an off-chain rate — **a trusted input**: by hand at launch, then re-priced every week, in the 4 hours before the week's cohorts open, by the Operator's `crank chips publish --auto`, which reads the **Jupiter Price API** (mainnet SKR mint)
weaknesses.why: The contract must never read a price
weaknesses.fix: On-chain chip governance before real value is at stake

weaknesses.what: Cohorts are filled by real members first; scripted members — real wallets under the same contract rules, whose forfeits fund real prizes and whose completed days are **not camera-verified** — top a cohort up only to a minimum (10 in a short test round, within a minute of a real member joining it; none in a 7-day or 21-day one)
weaknesses.why: A cohort must never be empty when someone installs the app during judging, and a judge who joins a short test round should not run it alone
weaknesses.fix: Disclosed here, in the app, in the demo video and in the pitch deck; their addresses are published in the build and every scripted member is labelled wherever it appears

weaknesses.what: A wallet is required before anything, even the Daily 25
weaknesses.why: One identity from the first tap; guest mode was considered and dropped
weaknesses.fix: The connect screen says how to get a wallet; the demo video, sent with the submission, shows the whole product without one

weaknesses.what: The faucet's fee sponsor key ships inside the app
weaknesses.why: A wallet with zero SOL cannot pay for its own first transaction, and there is no server to sign for it
weaknesses.fix: Anyone can extract the key, and empty the 0.05 SOL float it holds, so the contract bounds that instead of assuming it will not happen: no wallet is limited (a tester who runs out may claim again), but a single daily budget of 0.72 SOL covering **every** lamport that leaves the faucet — top-ups and reimbursements alike — and a permissionless refill, so a drained sponsor is restored by the next crank pass rather than ending onboarding. Real fix: no faucet on mainnet, or a rate-limited relayer

weaknesses.what: The program keeps its upgrade authority during judging
weaknesses.why: A defect found while cohort #3 holds real test stakes must be fixable
weaknesses.fix: Used only for defect fixes that change no existing cohort, account layout or fund movement. Real fix: revoke the authority once the contract is final

weaknesses.what: The fee funds a comeback pledge, a developer share and operations by rule, but the developer and operations shares are ordinary wallets
weaknesses.why: Of every forfeited stake, 10% is set aside as the forfeiting member's own comeback, in the league's reserve vault, which only the program can move (a comeback nobody makes good, and the pool of a Holdout nobody finished, feed that league's boost reserve there), and 10% and 10% go to the developer and operations wallets named in this README (H35; re-split 2026-10-12, H39). What those two wallets then do with it is not enforced by the contract
weaknesses.fix: Publish both wallets' addresses and their spending; later, move operations spending on chain or under a multisig

weaknesses.what: Spark Holdouts count push-ups from the knees on thin evidence
weaknesses.why: Knees-allowed counting at 45 degrees was measured on about 26 recordings from mostly one person: 87% of honest knee reps counted, 3 of 56 cobras slipped through - 2 of them filmed at about 30 degrees, which the Spark camera check now refuses (H35)
weaknesses.fix: Record at least 3 people, 100 knee reps and cobras at 30-60 degrees, and replay them before any real money rides on Spark

weaknesses.what: A Daily 25 done before the phone has ever read chain time is dated afterwards, from the phone's own uptime clock
weaknesses.why: The Daily 25 needs no connection, but a day is chain time (05:00 UTC), never the phone's clock. The last chain reading is kept, so this only happens after a reboot with no network since. Several such sittings are dated together, from the latest one's start; reps done offline across a reboot stay undated
weaknesses.fix: Keep one record per offline sitting and date each separately

weaknesses.what: Reminders are on-device only — no push
weaknesses.why: No server knows anyone's deadlines. The phone schedules a reminder when a Holdout starts, halfway through each day (with sound) and before its deadline (silently), from chain time, and a day you have done that is not on chain yet stays in the notification shade and is re-posted silently every hour until it is submitted (FR-068). A Holdout you finished gets one notice 15 minutes after its end, when settlement usually has come; it does not check the chain, so it says your claim is *probably* ready (FR-068b). Android may deliver them a few minutes late, not at all after a restart until the app is opened, and never if notifications are declined. The deadline is the chain's, never the reminder's
weaknesses.fix: A push service fed by the chain, alongside the on-device reminders

weaknesses.what: One key, `operator.json`, is both the crank's fee payer and the only key that can publish the chip set, and it sits as a hot secret on the Fly machine that runs the crank (and in the GitHub Actions fallback)
weaknesses.why: Opening a round every 30 minutes in two test lobbies needs a funded payer. A separate payer key was considered and the product owner decided against it (2026-10-11, L14), so this is an accepted risk of the devnet build, not an oversight. Whoever takes the key can re-price the stakes of every Holdout not yet open and spend its float. Worse, it can publish one chip set with an enormous top tier: the program keeps the highest top tier ever published (`max_top_tier` only rises) and the faucet mints exactly that much per claim, and `Config.operator` has no rotation instruction. The faucet then mints absurd amounts or fails, new wallets lose their way to SKR, and only a program upgrade undoes it. The same machine and the GitHub Actions fallback also hold the keypairs of the 56 scripted members (`HOLDOUT_SCRIPTED_KEYS_TGZ_B64`), so a compromise can stop their submissions (forfeits that move real pools), join or leave, and claim their payouts. What it cannot do is touch a real member's stake or a settled payout, which only the program moves
weaknesses.fix: A payer key of its own holding only the float, an operator key kept off the machine (or a multisig), an operator rotation instruction and a cap on the top tier, and the scripted keys held apart, for the mainnet build
